title: NVIDIA CUDA — mount and forward
why: Run a Go layer on NVIDIA GPU with an explicit lifetime.
what: Mount an identity Dense layer, inspect the CUDA version and device identity, and forward a Float32 tensor.
body_extra:
Session ownership

Create a session with nativecuda.Mount, call Forward repeatedly and close it when finished. Mount accepts supported layers, Stack, Parallel and Grid layouts. The library is independent of welvet.cpp and welvet.metal.

Requirements and backend boundaries

Go Welvet v1.4.0 uses the independent welvet.cuda 0.79 library (mounted model ABI 1). Install from its checkout:

cd ../welvet.cuda
./scripts/linux_install_go.sh
# Windows amd64 (MSVC + CUDA Toolkit):
./scripts/windows_install_go.ps1

Execution requires Linux x86_64 or Windows amd64, Go with cgo, and an NVIDIA driver/runtime. Set WELVET_CUDA_LIBRARY to override library discovery. On Windows, ensure the CUDA runtime (cudart) resolves via PATH. Ordinary Go CPU use does not require an NVIDIA GPU. Unsupported hosts print SKIP; missing libraries or no GPU on a supported host also soft-SKIP in these book examples.

Go schedules work and manages memory; numerical CUDA forward, backward and weight updates execute device kernels. Activations are Float32; FormatNone parameter storage follows the CUDA dtype matrix. Small examples demonstrate APIs; GPU launch costs can outweigh useful work at small shapes.

cpu-tiled / go_cpu means Go CPU; native_cpu means welvet.cpp; cuda means the independent NVIDIA GPU library. Examples 89–93 can use go run -tags welvet_cuda . to exclude C++ linkage. Chapter 94 requires the normal cgo build for both native engines. JSON routing (§93–§94) is Linux amd64 today; explicit Mount works on Windows amd64 as well.

title: NVIDIA CUDA — Mamba parameter dtypes
why: Exercise native storage formats without changing the activation interface.
what: Run a seeded Mamba forward pass across all 34 native parameter dtypes, or select one with -dtype.
body_extra:
Storage versus arithmetic

-dtype all sweeps native parameter representations. The CUDA execution interface uses Float32 activations. Quantized FormatNone dtype storage and packed quantization formats are different coverage claims.

go run . -dtype all
go run . -dtype float16

Requirements and library installation (Linux + Windows): chapter 89.

title: NVIDIA CUDA — training modes
why: Keep repeated training updates in the mounted CUDA session.
what: Train two Dense layers using one of the 29 numbered modes, with persistent Step Line state and real Grid layouts for Mesh modes.
body_extra:
Training families

-mode all exercises all 29 modes. Step modes retain their Line session across calls. Mesh modes use a three-cell Grid with disabled ingress and two active layers, advancing four ticks per call. Bundled welvet.cuda 0.79 covers train modes through StepTweenSplitSparse. These small demonstrations validate usage; they are not performance measurements.

go run . -mode NormalBP -steps 8
go run . -mode all -steps 8

Explicit mounted sessions keep updated weights native until SyncToGo(). Close discards any updates not returned to Go. See chapter 92 before saving.

Requirements: chapter 89.

title: NVIDIA CUDA — weight return and ENTITY save
why: Return trained weights to Go before executing or saving the Go model.
what: Train natively, explicitly SyncToGo, save an ENTITY, reload it and compare the native parameter snapshots.
body_extra:
Weight handoff

session, err := nativecuda.Mount(layer)
// Check err; defer session.Close().
// Repeat session.TrainMSE(...) as needed.
err = session.SyncToGo()
// Check err, then save through Go ENTITY IO.

Mount copies model state into a native session. The original Go parameters stay unchanged while that explicit session trains. SyncToGo() returns parameter bytes, scales and Float64 biases for Go saving. This saves model parameters, not a portable checkpoint of live Line, proxy, KV or rule state.

Use -out /path/model.entity to choose the output location. The default uses a temporary directory and prints it.

Requirements: chapter 89.

title: NVIDIA CUDA — JSON backend placement
why: Choose which layers run on NVIDIA GPU while retaining ordinary Go training entry points.
what: Enable the CUDA router and apply JSON placement to a Stack: layer 0 on Go CPU, layers 1–2 on CUDA.
body_extra:
Explicit placement

The example embeds placement.json; use -config to load another file. nativecuda.EnableRouting() installs the router for its owner lifetime (Linux amd64). placement.Stack applies immediate-child numeric layer keys.

Routed execution maintains native sessions and returns updated parameters to Go automatically. Changing source weights remounts a session and resets transient native state. Automatic hardware/performance planning remains separate from explicit placement.

Windows amd64 supports explicit Mount (chapters 89–92); automatic JSON routing is Linux-only in this release.

Requirements: chapter 89.

title: NVIDIA CUDA — mixed Go/C++/CUDA
why: Split a single model between the independent native engines and Go.
what: Run a 13-layer Dense Stack: Go layers 0–3, C++ layers 4–8 and CUDA layers 9–12; verify actual native calls during training.
body_extra:
Three engines in one Go model

Go CPU [0–3] → welvet.cpp [4–8] → welvet.cuda [9–12] → Go result

The embedded placement.json uses go_cpu, native_cpu and cuda. Install both native libraries and use the normal cgo build (do not pass -tags welvet_cuda). The example reports successful C++ C ABI calls and CUDA routing counters after five NormalBP updates.

Activations and parameters cross backend boundaries. Live backend-specific Line, proxy, KV or rule state is not migrated between engines.

Requirements: Linux amd64 + chapter 89.

title: NVIDIA CUDA — results and suite pointers
why: Find live CUDA parity/timing matrices after the small usage chapters.
what: Print Go v1.4.0 / welvet.cuda 0.79 pins and commands for w2a go_v_cuda and cuda_smoke. No GPU required.
body_extra:
Where live results live

This chapter is host-only. It does not claim timings from loading the page. Run the sibling matrices on a machine with an NVIDIA GPU:

cd ../../w2a && go test ./tests/go_v_cuda -count=1 -timeout 180m
cd ../../welvet.cuda/examples/cuda_smoke && go run .
cd welvet/examples && ./run_nvidia.sh

Engine pin: welvet.cuda 0.79, model ABI 1, Go binding nativecuda (Welvet v1.4.0). Platforms: Linux x86_64 + Windows amd64 for Mount; Linux amd64 for EnableRouting.

Requirements overview: chapter 89.
